brief: Localize Foreman's documentation for our Korean freelancers. Milestone 1 (0.05 USDC): README.ko.md, a complete and natural Korean translation of README.md that keeps every section including the limits table, submitted as a pull request to github.com/yangdongsuk/foreman. Milestone 2 (0.15 USDC): a Korean landing page published at https://yangdongsuk.github.io/foreman/ko.html that explains how Foreman works, lists the limits the contract enforces, and links to the dashboard and the Korean README. Three days per milestone.

plan.title: Korean localization of Foreman documentation
plan.summary: Two sequential milestones: (1) a complete Korean README.ko.md submitted as a pull request to yangdongsuk/foreman, and (2) a Korean landing page at https://yangdongsuk.github.io/foreman/ko.html explaining how Foreman works, listing enforced contract limits, and linking to the dashboard and the Korean README. Total 0.2 USDC, 3 days per milestone.
plan.reasoning: The work splits naturally into the translation (milestone 1) and the landing page (milestone 2), which depends on it because the page must link to the Korean README. Amounts follow the owner's brief (0.05 and 0.15 USDC, summing exactly to the 0.2 budget). Milestone 2 at 0.15 exceeds the 0.1 USDC agent auto-approval threshold, so it needs the owner's co-signature. The brief gave that split, and it is kept rather than distorted. Criteria are written to be checkable from the public PR diff and the live page text and links.

milestones.name: Korean README
milestones.deliverable: A GitHub pull request URL to github.com/yangdongsuk/foreman that adds README.ko.md, a complete Korean translation of README.md.
acceptanceCriteria: The pull request targets the yangdongsuk/foreman repository and adds a file named README.ko.md at the repository root.
README.ko.md contains a Korean heading or section corresponding to every heading in the current README.md, in the same order, with none omitted.
The limits table from README.md is present in README.ko.md as a Markdown table with the same rows and numeric values as the original, with labels and descriptions translated into Korean.
The prose of README.ko.md is written in Korean (Hangul) rather than left in English, apart from code blocks, commands, URLs, and product or technical names such as Foreman and USDC.
Code blocks, commands and links in README.ko.md match those in README.md, and the pull request changes no file other than README.ko.md, apart from an optional link to it in README.md.

milestones.name: Korean landing page
milestones.deliverable: The live URL https://yangdongsuk.github.io/foreman/ko.html, publicly reachable, with its source added to the repository (a PR or commit link may be provided as supporting evidence).
acceptanceCriteria: Fetching https://yangdongsuk.github.io/foreman/ko.html returns HTTP 200 and the visible page text is primarily Korean (Hangul).

The page has a section, with a Korean heading, that explains how Foreman works in steps, covering at least: the brief or plan, USDC escrow of milestones, submission of a deliverable, automated review, and payment on approval.
The page lists the limits the contract enforces, with the same values as the limits table in README.md, expressed in Korean.
The page contains a hyperlink to the Foreman dashboard, using the same dashboard URL given in README.md.
The page contains a hyperlink to the Korean README, pointing to README.ko.md in the yangdongsuk/foreman repository on GitHub.

risks: Milestone 2 (0.15 USDC) exceeds the 0.1 USDC agent auto-approval limit, so it requires the owner's co-signature, which may delay payout.
The brief does not say where the dashboard URL is. The plan assumes it is in README.md, so if it is not, the freelancer needs it supplied.
"Complete and natural" translation quality is only partly checkable by an automated reviewer. The criteria focus on structural completeness, so awkward Korean may still pass.
Milestone 2 depends on README.ko.md being merged or at least at a stable public URL. If the PR is not merged, the link to the Korean README may return 404 at review time.
GitHub Pages publication depends on repository settings and build delays. The freelancer needs write or deploy access, or the owner must merge and publish promptly.
The README.md may change between the start of work and review, which could cause section mismatches. Review should compare against the version at funding time.
Fixed three-day deadlines for each milestone run from funding, so milestone 2 cannot realistically start until milestone 1 is done unless the freelancer works in parallel.
